texto:
Salesforce on October 20, 2026 signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze, the New York-based customer engagement platform, for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value, with holders of Braze Class A common stock set to receive $47.50 in cash per share. The deal, which still needs Braze shareholder approval and regulatory clearance, is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal year 2028.
In Short
Salesforce, which sells software that companies use to manage customers and send marketing, has agreed to buy Braze, a company whose software sends app notifications, emails and text messages based on what people do in real time. The two companies are among the largest vendors of tools that brands use to message their customers, so the deal concentrates a big part of that market in one owner. Nothing changes for Braze customers until the deal closes, which Salesforce expects no earlier than February 2027, and only after shareholders and regulators sign off.
The terms
The headline figure is an enterprise value of approximately $5.66 billion. Under the agreement, according to Salesforce, holders of Braze Class A common stock will receive $47.50 in cash per share. The release, distributed through Business Wire with a San Francisco and New York dateline, does not state the premium that price represents over Braze's recent trading, does not describe how Salesforce will finance the purchase, and does not give the size of any termination fee.
That last omission is partial. The forward-looking statements section lists among the risks "the risk that the merger agreement may be terminated in circumstances requiring Salesforce or Braze to pay a termination fee," which confirms that the agreement contains such a fee for both sides. The amount will appear in regulatory filings rather than in the announcement. The release also flags "the possibility that competing offers may be made" as a risk factor, a standard line in public-company merger documents but one that leaves the door formally open until the shareholder vote.
Only Class A shares are named in the per-share terms. Braze has a dual-class structure, and the release does not say how Class B shares will be treated.
The closing timeline is long. According to Salesforce, the transaction is expected to close in its fiscal year 2028, "subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Braze's shareholders and receipt of required regulatory approvals." Salesforce's fiscal year ends on January 31, which means fiscal 2028 begins on February 1, 2027. On that reading, the earliest the deal could close is a little over three months from the announcement, and it could run considerably longer.
Salesforce said there is "no anticipated change" to its fiscal 2027 guidance. It has not issued guidance for fiscal 2028, and there is no update to long-term targets "at this time."
Advisors and filings
J.P. Morgan Securities LLC is serving as exclusive financial advisor to Salesforce, with Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and Covington & Burling LLP as legal counsel. On the other side, Qatalyst Partners is the exclusive financial advisor to Braze, and Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP is its legal counsel.
Braze intends to file a preliminary proxy statement on Schedule 14A with the Securities and Exchange Commission, followed by a definitive proxy to be delivered to shareholders. That document is where the premium calculation, the background of the negotiations, any competing approaches and the fee amounts are likely to be disclosed. Braze's 2026 annual meeting proxy, filed with the SEC on May 18, 2026, is cited in the release as the source for information about its directors and executive officers.
What the price implies
Braze reported $738.2 million in revenue for its fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, up 24%. On PPC Land's own calculation, an enterprise value of $5.66 billion is roughly 7.7 times that trailing annual revenue figure. Braze went public in November 2021 at $65 per share. The $47.50 cash price sits about 27% below that IPO price, again by PPC Land's calculation. Neither comparison appears in the Salesforce release, and neither says anything about the premium over the shares' price before the announcement, which the release does not disclose.
What Braze does
Braze was founded in New York in 2011 as Appboy by Bill Magnuson, Jon Hyman and Mark Ghermezian, and was renamed in 2017. The release describes Braze as a platform that helps marketers respond "to customer behavior in real time, coordinating personalized experiences across mobile apps, websites, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and more."
The technical description is specific. According to Salesforce, Braze's "cloud-native, event-streaming architecture is optimized for high-volume, real-time B2C engagement, continuously updating customer profiles and adapting customer journeys while powering trillions of messages and journey actions each year." Event streaming, in this context, means that customer actions such as opening an app, browsing a product or abandoning a cart are processed as they happen rather than in periodic batches, and those signals update the profile and the next message a customer receives.
BrazeAI, the company's AI layer, extends that with what the release calls "AI-powered optimization across content, offers, channels, and timing." Much of that decisioning capability came from OfferFit, a reinforcement learning company that Braze agreed to buy on March 27, 2025, for $325 million in cash and Class A stock, closing on June 2, 2025. Braze's product line also includes Canvas, a journey builder; Liquid, a templating language for personalization; Currents, a paid add-on for exporting event data; Audience Sync, which sends audiences to ad platforms such as Google and Facebook; and the Braze Data Platform with Cloud Data Ingestion.
Customers and scale
According to the release, Braze serves approximately 2,770 customers, including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban Outfitters and Venmo. As of the quarter ended April 30, 2026, Braze had reported 2,713 customers, 349 of which had annual recurring revenue of $500,000 or more. The difference suggests a net addition of about 57 customers in the months since, though the release uses "approximately" and does not give a reporting date.
The company is headquartered in New York with 15 offices across the Americas, EMEA and APAC, according to its boilerplate.
How Salesforce plans to use it
Salesforce frames the deal around a four-part architecture. "Following the close of the transaction," the release states, "Braze's real-time engagement and AI decisioning capabilities are expected to complement all four layers of Salesforce's architecture - Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and SIForce." The fourth name, SIForce, does not appear in earlier PPC Land coverage of Salesforce's platform. When Salesforce described its stack at its TDX developer conference on April 15, 2026, Data 360 was the system of context, Customer 360 the system of work, Agentforce the system of agency and Slack the system of engagement. The release does not explain what SIForce is or whether it replaces Slack in that framing.
Within Customer 360, the stated target is Marketing Cloud. According to Salesforce, Braze "is expected to strengthen Marketing Cloud's cross-channel personalization, helping brands turn a deeper view of each customer into richer experiences, optimized in real time at the scale needed to reach hundreds of millions of people."
Marketing Cloud has its own acquisition history. Its foundation was ExactTarget, the martech company Salesforce bought for $2.5 billion on June 4, 2013. Braze, built more than a decade later around mobile apps and event data, has competed directly with that product for years. Gartner placed Braze, Salesforce and Adobe as the three Leaders in its 2025 Magic Quadrant for Multichannel Marketing Hubs. The agreement therefore puts two of the three Leaders in that category under one owner.
Three stated outcomes
The release lists three things Salesforce and Braze "would help businesses" do together:
- Act on customer behavior in real time. According to Salesforce, Braze's event-streaming architecture "turns live customer signals and data from cloud data warehouses and other platforms into personalized messages and coordinated journeys."
- Deliver richer experiences across channels. Braze's mobile and app capabilities, "including in-app messages, personalized content feeds, and live updates," are described as working alongside email, web and messaging channels.
- Make personalization more intelligent. Braze's AI decisioning optimizes content, offers, channels and timing, and the release says combining that with "Salesforce's customer context and Agentforce" would connect marketing "with the broader customer relationship across commerce, sales, and service."
The reference to cloud data warehouses is notable. It points to a model in which customer data stays in a warehouse such as Snowflake or Databricks and is read by the engagement layer, rather than being copied wholesale into a marketing database. The release states that both companies "share a commitment to an open, composable approach that gives customers flexibility across the data, tools, and partners they rely on." Whether that holds once Braze sits inside a vendor that also sells Data 360 as its own data layer is one of the questions the announcement leaves open.
What the executives said
Patrick Stokes, President, Applications and Marketing at Salesforce, put the case in terms of timing. "Every interaction is an opportunity to wow your customers," Stokes said. "Most of that wow comes from knowing your customer, and responding at just the right moment. Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. Bringing that capability together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction."
Bill Magnuson, CEO and co-founder of Braze, signalled that the brand would survive the acquisition. "Braze was built on the conviction that marketers and their creativity are a brand's ultimate competitive advantage," he said. "This past year we shipped at the fastest pace in our history, and BrazeAI is helping marketers get their best ideas live faster. Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we'll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who built this company with us. Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers."
"Continue building as Braze" is the only indication in the release about how the product will be positioned after closing. The release does not say whether Braze will be sold as a separate product, merged into Marketing Cloud, or offered as a tier within it, and it gives no detail on pricing, contract terms or roadmap for existing customers of either platform. According to Salesforce, Magnuson and co-founder Jon Hyman lead the company and would "bring deep expertise in mobile experiences, data engineering, and customer engagement to Salesforce Marketing Cloud." No retention terms for either founder are disclosed.
A run of deals
The Braze agreement is the latest in a sequence of purchases. Salesforce agreed on May 27, 2025, to buy Informatica for $8 billion and completed that deal on November 18, 2025. Earlier, Salesforce paid about $700 million for Krux in October 2016.
The pace in 2026 has been faster still. Salesforce acquired Qualified in April 2026 for about $1.2 billion, and in June 2026 reached an agreement for Intercom reported at about $3.6 billion, with both companies' products now appearing as prebuilt agents named Piper and Fin, as PPC Land reported when Salesforce unveiled seven prebuilt agents on September 11. Smaller purchases covered by PPC Land include Zoomin, PredictSpring and Doti.
The release places Braze inside an explicit framework. Salesforce says it pursues "acquisitions that meet the standards of our M&A framework: advancing customer success, fitting within our strategy, accelerating innovation, and creating long-term value." It also states that "AI is raising the bar for marketers, who now need agentic solutions that can understand customers, make decisions, and act in real time."
Is this a data deal, an AI deal or a channel deal? The release presents it as all three. In practical terms, the clearest gap Braze fills is mobile: push notifications, in-app messages and live updates, delivered at consumer scale from live event data. That is the area where Braze built its business as Appboy, and where it is typically positioned as an enterprise engagement platform that works alongside an external data layer rather than as a database of record.
Why it matters for marketers
Consolidation in the martech market has been running for years. Scott Brinker's 2026 landscape counted 15,505 vendors, with removals (1,367) nearly matching additions (1,488) for the first time in 15 years. Large engagement-layer platforms have been part of that. Canva bought Ortto, a customer data and marketing automation company with more than 11,000 customers, on April 8, 2026, and Adobe completed its $1.9 billion purchase of Semrush on April 28, 2026. Publicis agreed to buy LiveRamp for $2.5 billion on May 17, 2026.
For the roughly 2,770 brands using Braze, several practical issues follow from the release, and the release resolves none of them. The first is the CRM and data-layer question: many Braze customers run it on top of their own warehouse or a non-Salesforce data stack, and the "open, composable" language in the release is a statement of intent, not a contractual commitment. The second is overlap with Marketing Cloud, which offers its own journey orchestration, email and mobile messaging. The third is competition. With Braze and Salesforce under one owner, the remaining independent enterprise engagement platforms include Iterable, which PPC Land has described as Braze's closest direct comparator, and Adobe, the other Leader in Gartner's 2025 quadrant.
The regulatory review is the other variable. The release refers only to "required regulatory approvals" without naming jurisdictions. A combination of two Leaders in one analyst category is the kind of overlap competition authorities examine, although the market for customer engagement software is fragmented and contested by many smaller vendors.
Salesforce has been arguing for months that agents, not people, will increasingly be the interface for both marketers and consumers. One day before this deal, a Salesforce executive argued that personal AI agents will send more traffic to business contact centers, not less, and the company has spent the year connecting outside data to its agents, including Demandbase intent data inside its Hunter sales agent. Braze adds the outbound half of that picture: the system that decides which message reaches a consumer, on which channel, and when. Salesforce's own wording describes this as engagement "optimized in real time at the scale needed to reach hundreds of millions of people." How much of that scale moves onto Salesforce's own data layer, and how much stays in customers' existing warehouses, will be visible only after closing.

Summary
Who: Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) and Braze (NASDAQ: BRZE), with Salesforce's Patrick Stokes and Braze CEO and co-founder Bill Magnuson quoted. J.P. Morgan advises Salesforce and Qatalyst Partners advises Braze.
What: A definitive agreement for Salesforce to acquire Braze for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value, paying $47.50 in cash per Braze Class A share. Braze's real-time engagement and AI decisioning tools are expected to strengthen Marketing Cloud and connect to Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce and SIForce.
When: Announced on October 20, 2026. Closing is expected in Salesforce's fiscal year 2028, which begins February 1, 2027, subject to Braze shareholder approval and regulatory approvals.
Where: The release carries a San Francisco and New York dateline. Braze is headquartered in New York with 15 offices across the Americas, EMEA and APAC and serves about 2,770 customers.
Why: Salesforce says marketers need agentic tools that can understand customers, make decisions and act in real time, and that Braze's event-streaming architecture and mobile capabilities fill that role. For the market, the deal places two of the three Leaders in Gartner's 2025 quadrant for multichannel marketing hubs under one owner and leaves open how Braze's composable, warehouse-friendly model fits beside Salesforce's own data layer.
